minutes.headline: Finance Committee recommended most special Town Meeting articles but opposed the Wallace Park playground money.
minutes.summary: The committee held a public hearing on the special Town Meeting warrant, hearing the town manager, finance director and petitioners on each article. It then voted recommendations: approval on the budget adjustment, the TC Passios design, the revolving funds, the Chase Road deed, the tower lease and the tax agreement. It recommended disapproval of the citizen petition for Wallace Park playground money. Several articles were judged to have no direct financial impact.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to recommend disapproval of the citizen petition for Wallace Park playground money, though the vote was not audible in the recording.
The committee voted to recommend approval of the FY18 budget adjustment, which adds to the reserve fund to cover snow and ice deficits.
It recommended approval of the TC Passios conceptual design, the four revolving fund articles, the Chase Road deed, the tower lease and the tax agreement.
The committee agreed that articles with no direct financial impact will be reported as such without a vote.
The committee will give time at a next regular meeting to its review role on tax agreements.

why_it_matters: These recommendations go to voters at the special Town Meeting, where residents decide on the budget adjustment, the playground petition, the revolving funds and the tax agreement.
The solar tax agreement sets a fixed payment for 25 years with no escalation, and the turf field debt payment leaves little revenue to spare, so both affect long-term town finances.
watch_next: A next regular Finance Committee meeting, where the committee plans to discuss its review role on tax agreements.
The special Town Meeting vote on the warrant articles, including the Wallace Park playground petition.
